definitions.explanation: A counter for number of times or frequency of events. Used to count how many times something happens or has happened.

examples.japanese: {一|いち}{日|にち}に{三|さん}{回|かい}{薬|くすり}を{飲|の}んでください。
examples.english: Please take the medicine three times a day.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}には{何|なん}{回|かい}{行|い}きましたか。
examples.english: How many times have you been to Japan?

examples.japanese: もう{一|いっ}{回|かい}{言|い}ってください。
examples.english: Please say it one more time.
examples.notes: Note: いっかい with small っ

examples.japanese: {今|いま}{週|しゅう}はもう{二|に}{回|かい}{映画|えいが}を{見|み}ました。
examples.english: I've already seen two movies this week.

examples.japanese: {一|いっ}{回|かい}しか{会|あ}ったことがないのに、{友達|ともだち}になりました。
examples.english: We became friends even though we only met once.

notes:
{回|かい} is the standard counter for occurrences, repetitions, or frequency.

COUNTING:
- {一|いっ}{回|かい}: once (note: いっかい with small っ)
- {二|に}{回|かい}: twice
- {三|さん}{回|かい}: three times
- {何|なん}{回|かい}: how many times?

PRONUNCIATION NOTE:
{一回|いっかい} uses gemination (small っ). It is NOT read いちかい.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- もう{一|いっ}{回|かい}: one more time
- {毎回|まいかい}: every time
- {初回|しょかい}: first time/round
- {今回|こんかい}: this time
- {次回|じかい}: next time

USAGE:
Often used with {〜に|に} to show frequency: {週|しゅう}に{三|さん}{回|かい} (three times a week).
